title: Storm timing showed a surface temperature contrast but no clear bleaching contrast in pooled reef records from 2003 to 2019
abstract: We linked Reef Check surveys to dated tropical storm tracks to test whether prior storms had lower bleaching associations than later storms. A model with site, ocean-year and ocean-month effects used 6,448 survey days at 1,452 sites in three oceans from 2003 to 2019. The prior-minus-later bleaching contrast was -0.92 percentage points, with a 95% interval of -3.25 to +1.42. All five estimable ocean-period bleaching intervals included zero after correction for six tests. The later Indian Ocean contrast could not be estimated. A secondary model of weekly surface temperature anomalies gave a pooled contrast of -0.397 C, with an interval of -0.557 to -0.236 C. This contrast remained negative in pooled sensitivity checks. The only clear adjusted regional surface result included zero after removal of windows near unknown storm intensity. The surface result fits a cooling explanation. It does not establish a causal cooling effect or coral protection. Selected visits, missing intensity, few regional clusters, coarse surface temperature and limited high-heat samples restrict inference. The package gives the dated linkage dataset, missing-value evidence, raw source hashes, all estimates, code, figures and numerical checks. It does not measure pollution or species loss.

display.caption: Prior-minus-later storm contrasts for bleaching and surface temperature anomaly. A storm point must be within 300 km, 1-30 days before or after a survey. The intervals have a six-test correction within each outcome. Grey marks sparse exposure. The later Indian Ocean contrast cannot be estimated. The surface test is secondary.

Pooled storm timing contrasts under alternate distance, timing, fixed-effect, and quality rules. All bleaching intervals include zero. Surface anomaly intervals are below zero. These are nominal 95% intervals. Surface sensitivity and missing-intensity checks were added after the primary fits.

citations.reason: The published cyclone-count scope warning motivates an actual dated-storm test. We rebuild the coral panel from raw data. The underlying coral archive overlaps; fitted data and estimates are not reused.
CoRTAD version 6 supplies the temperature fields already present in the coral compilation. We do not retrieve the gridded archive directly.
The pooled surface association is consistent with the cooling mechanism. This study does not identify the causal effect or independently validate the Florida result.
Legacy version 1 field definitions only. The analyzed raw release is version 2, recorded separately.
